correction: The auditor's PARTIAL status and the three remaining gaps hold (worktree and chat-folder first sends, native mobile, no eviction or latency measurement). Their fixDefects claim, "No correctness bug seen in the adopt/stop/expire paths", is wrong. The claim path in ensureSessionForThread ignores options.computerCatalogChanged. Prewarm fires on composer focus, before the user can type /computer-use. So a computer-use first turn on a new, stopped or reaped thread adopts a session whose Agent Control tool catalog was fixed at boot without the computer tools. A minor inaccuracy: makeRoom evicts the oldest ready entry, so browsing does not just hit the caps; each visit retires a warm process and spawns a new one. The concurrency race I suspected between two prewarms of one thread is harmless, because ProviderService.startSession stops the previous runtime of the same thread.
summary: Prewarm is implemented. 440c42224, 65c7e6f2d, a8a683529 and 3cbe9a677 added an owner-gated provider.prewarmSession RPC, a server pool (2 per instance, 4 overall, 2-minute TTL), adopt-or-stop at the turn start through a shared start key, and web triggers on composer focus and the first keystroke. A send adopts the warm session. Claude's query() spawns the CLI and sends initialize eagerly, so the CLI boot overlaps with typing. Codex startSession awaits initialize and thread/start. Still not covered: sends that first create a worktree or chat folder (the default env mode is local, so this is opt-in worktree users only), and the native mobile app, which never calls the RPC. There is also a regression the auditor missed. The claim path skips the computer-catalog restart check, so a /computer-use first turn adopts a prewarmed session whose MCP tools were listed before the computer plan was staged.

evidence.note: prewarm(): resolveStart and then providerService.startSession unbound from orchestration. Pool limits are at lines 74-76. makeRoom (158-180) retires the oldest ready entry, so each new prewarm past the cap kills a warm process and spawns another.
Requires an existing cwd. A draft that first creates a worktree or chat folder can never be prewarmed server-side.
claim() compares threadProviderStartKey only. The key (threadProviderStart.ts:78-87) has no computer-use or catalog dimension.
With no live session the claim path adopts the prewarm unconditionally. options.computerCatalogChanged is honoured only for existing sessions (line 1007), not here.
computerCatalogChanged is computed, and stageComputerTurn runs (1305), right before ensureSessionForThread (1317). A fresh start would boot with the plan staged; an adopted prewarm booted without it.
descriptorsFor adds the computer tools only when computerTurnPlan(threadId) is staged at tools/list time.

The Agent Control MCP advertises listChanged:false, and tools/list (265) is evaluated when the CLI connects at boot. A prewarmed Claude or Codex session keeps the catalog without computer tools for the claimed turn.

OpenCode installs the computer lease (2178-2184) only when the plan is staged at startSession. A prewarmed OpenCode session therefore has no computer lease. This fails closed (no authority leak) but breaks the computer-use turn.
The prewarm tests cover adopt, mid-start wait, mismatch, idle expiry, cursor discard, pool limit and drafts. None covers a computer-use turn adopting a prewarm.

createQuery is called at startSession. In SDK 0.3.296, ProcessTransport spawns in its constructor (or right after async prep when deferSpawn is set), and Query sends initialize eagerly. awaitCliInitialized (5929) then resolves at once on the first turn of a warm session.
startSession stops the thread's previous runtime before starting a new one. Orphans from racing prewarms or from handoff starts are cleaned up.
The RPC is ownerEffect-gated. The capability is advertised at apps/server/src/environment/Layers/ServerEnvironment.ts:102.
The web trigger returns early for shouldCreateWorktree or shouldMaterializeLegacyBranchWorktree, and for pending chats at 5228. The only caller of requestProviderSessionPrewarm is at 5245.

The composer is auto-focused on every activeThread.id change. That reaches onFocusCapture (ChatComposer.tsx:2756) with no dwell delay, so browsing threads prewarms each visited stopped thread. The first-keystroke trigger is at ChatComposer.tsx:1579.

Shared client throttle: a repeat of the same request within 30 s and any request for one thread within 3 s are dropped. apps/mobile has no caller; the only prewarm references there are route and highlighter prewarm.
defaultThreadEnvMode defaults to local, so the worktree gap only affects users who opt into worktree mode.
The 5-minute reaper is unchanged. Focus or the first keystroke on a reaped thread re-prewarms it, but only if the prompt was empty or the composer is refocused.

remaining:
1. Worktree and chat-folder first sends are never prewarmed. The web client skips them at apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:5228 and 5243, and the server needs an existing cwd at ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:203. Users who opt into worktree mode still pay the full Claude or Codex start on the first turn.
2. The native mobile app (apps/mobile), the intended phone surface, never calls requestProviderSessionPrewarm (packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/sessionPrewarm.ts:35).
3. Minor gaps:
   - No eviction on memory pressure or settings change.
   - No dwell delay on focus-triggered prewarm, so browsing threads churns full-config CLI processes (ChatView.tsx:3345 plus makeRoom at ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:158).
   - No real latency measurement; only a mocked one at ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts:7625.
fixDefects:
Regression: a computer-use first turn adopts a prewarmed session that lacks the computer tools.

The path:
1. Opening or focusing a thread whose session is stopped or absent prewarms it (ChatView.tsx:3345, then onFocusCapture, then provider.prewarmSession).
2. The prewarmed CLI connects to the Agent Control MCP at boot and lists tools while no computer plan is staged, so computerBetaTools.ts:215 omits the computer descriptors. listChanged is false (agentControl/Mcp/listener.ts:254), so the list never refreshes.
3. When the user sends /computer-use, runTurnStart stages the plan and computes computerCatalogChanged=true (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1303-1316). ensureSessionForThread honours that flag only for an existing live session (line 1007). The no-session branch claims and binds the prewarm unconditionally (1119-1128).

Result: Claude and Codex run the turn without the computer tools. OpenCode never installed the computer lease (OpenCodeAdapter.ts:2134, 2178), and its host context says Agent Control without computer. This fails closed, with no authority leak, but the desktop beta computer-use feature breaks on the first turn of every new, stopped or reaped thread.

No test covers it (ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts:7576-7790).
implementationSketch:
A. Computer-use defect (do first; S effort, low risk).
- Add a `computerTurn: boolean` field to ThreadProviderStart.
- Include it in threadProviderStartKey (apps/server/src/orchestration/threadProviderStart.ts:78).
- In ProviderCommandReactor's desiredStart (around line 879), set it to `computerTurnPlan(threadId) !== undefined`. The plan is already staged before ensureSessionForThread.
- In ProviderSessionPrewarm.resolveStart (around line 221), set it the same way. In practice that is false at focus time.
- A computer turn then mismatches. claim() stops the warm runtime (and discards a never-run native conversation), and the turn starts fresh with the plan staged.
- Simpler alternative: in ensureSessionForThread, skip the claim when options.computerCatalogChanged or computerTurnPlan(threadId) is set. This needs an explicit retire of the entry, e.g. a new `discard(threadId)` on ProviderSessionPrewarmShape, so the warm process is not left until its TTL.
- Test in the "session prewarm" describe block (ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts:7576): prewarm, then dispatch a turn start with computerUse set. Assert two startSession calls, a stopSessionBinding on the prewarmed runtimeSessionId, and that the second start ran with the plan staged.

B. Native mobile prewarm (S-M effort, low risk).
- Extract the web gating policy (ChatView.tsx:5224-5255: no pending chat, dispatch allowed, no pending hosted target, session stopped or null, no worktree create or materialize, model, runtime and token mode) into a pure client-runtime helper next to requestProviderSessionPrewarm, e.g. `resolveProviderSessionPrewarmRequest(...)` in packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/sessionPrewarm.ts. Have ChatView use it.
- Call it from the mobile thread composer on editor focus and on the first non-empty change (apps/mobile/src/native/ComposerEditor.* as wired by the thread detail screen), gated on server config capabilities.providerSessionPrewarm.
- Unit-test the helper in sessionPrewarm.test.ts and add a mobile screen test asserting one RPC per focus.

C. Browse churn (S effort).
- Keep the first-keystroke trigger immediate, but delay the focus-triggered prewarm until the composer has held focus on the same thread for about 500-800 ms. Cancel on thread change or blur.
- Extend apps/web/src/components/ChatView.Prewarm.browser.tsx: rapid thread switching sends no RPC; dwelling sends exactly one.

D. Worktree-mode first turns (L effort).
- Either create the worktree speculatively at draft time, or prewarm only providers whose cwd can be rebound before the first turn.
- This is a product decision and is not recommended now.
decisionReason: Items A to C need no product, security or cross-repo decision. A is a correctness fix that restores pre-prewarm behaviour for computer-use turns. B and C reuse the existing owner-gated RPC and the existing throttle. Only the optional worktree extension (D) needs a product decision, because it means creating worktrees speculatively at draft time. There is no Hub change: the relay carries the RPC opaquely, and the Hub's vendored Ryco (7bc39eec3) already includes 440c42224 and 65c7e6f2d.
